front: When would you add a cache in front of a database?
back:
Reads far outnumber writes
The same rows are requested repeatedly
Slightly stale data is acceptable
The database is the latency or load bottleneck

front: Name the main cache write strategies and their trade-off.
back:
Write-through: consistent, slower writes
Write-back: fast writes, risk of data loss
Write-around: avoids polluting the cache, first read misses
Cache-aside: app controls loading, can serve stale data

front: What can a load balancer use to pick a server?
back:
Round robin
Least connections
Weighted capacity
Consistent hashing on a key
Health checks to drop failed servers

L4: routes on IP and port, fast, content-blind
L7: routes on URL, headers or cookies, can terminate TLS
L7 costs more CPU but allows smarter routing

front: When do you shard a database, and what goes wrong?
back:
Shard when one node cannot hold the data or the write load
Pick a key with even spread to avoid hot shards
Cross-shard joins and transactions get hard
Resharding is expensive, so plan for growth

front: List the ways to scale reads on a relational database.
back:
Add read replicas
Cache hot queries
Add the right indexes
Denormalise read-heavy views
Accept replica lag on replicas
